paragraphs: Here's what I see in this passage, friend. Manasseh had a godly father, and he still tore down everything that father built. He even set up an Asherah pole in the temple, the very place of which the LORD had said, "I will establish My Name forever." (2 Kings 21:7) A good example at home didn't make his choices for him, and that goes for you and me too.

Then look at what happens when nobody turns back. The LORD speaks through His servants the prophets, and He doesn't leave anybody guessing why the calamity is coming (2 Kings 21:10-15). Amon walks in all the ways of his father and abandons the LORD (2 Kings 21:21-22). Sin gets passed down like a family recipe, and nobody wants THAT recipe, friend.

So what do we carry out of this? Walking with the LORD is something each of us chooses, and it's not something we inherit. I think the quiet lesson is to listen when He speaks, because the people in this passage did not listen (2 Kings 21:9). Keep your ears open and your ovens ready, baker, because He is worth following.
